message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "interpret_cxr_volume_loss_patterns", "description": "When interpreting chest X-rays showing mediastinal shift and diaphragmatic elevation, prioritize volume loss as the unifying mechanism before considering primary diaphragmatic pathology or contralateral hyperinflation.", "applicable_conditions": "Chest X-ray interpretation tasks involving ipsilateral structural shifts (mediastinal deviation, hemidiaphragm elevation) where the underlying etiology may be ambiguous between volume loss, mass effect, or primary diaphragmatic dysfunction.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": ["chest_xray_classifier", "chest_xray_report_generator"], "risk_level": "medium", "core_action": "If the chest X-ray shows ipsilateral mediastinal shift and elevated hemidiaphragm: (1) use `chest_xray_classifier` to assess for signs of lung hypoplasia or atelectasis (volume loss); (2) explicitly rule out primary diaphragmatic paralysis or eventration only after volume loss is evaluated; (3) generate the final report using `chest_xray_report_generator` attributing the structural shifts to volume loss unless contradictory evidence exists."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
